definitions.explanation: In grammar, the verb form used to give direct commands or orders. In Japanese, formed by changing the verb ending (e.g., {食|た}べろ, {行|い}け).

examples.japanese: {命令形|めいれいけい}は{強|つよ}い{口調|くちょう}になる。
「{行|い}く」の{命令形|めいれいけい}は「{行|い}け」です。
{日本語|にほんご}の{命令形|めいれいけい}は{男性|だんせい}が{使|つか}うことが{多|おお}く、{女性|じょせい}は{丁寧|ていねい}な{表現|ひょうげん}を{好|この}む。
examples.english: The Japanese imperative form is more commonly used by men, while women tend to prefer polite expressions.

notes:
A grammar term composed of {命令|めいれい} (command, order) and {形|けい} (form). Refers to the conjugated form of Japanese verbs used for direct commands.

IMPERATIVE FORM BY VERB TYPE:
- {一段|いちだん} verbs: stem + ろ ({食|た}べる → {食|た}べろ)
- {五段|ごだん} verbs: え-row ending ({行|い}く → {行|い}け, {読|よ}む → {読|よ}め)
- する → しろ
- {来|く}る → {来|こ}い

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {命令形|めいれいけい}に{変|か}える: to change into the imperative form
- {命令形|めいれいけい}で{言|い}う: to say in the imperative form
- {命令形|めいれいけい}の{活用|かつよう}: conjugation of the imperative form

USAGE:
The bare imperative is considered rough and masculine in Japanese. It appears in sports cheering, emergency situations, and casual male speech. In formal or polite contexts, ～てください or ～なさい is used instead.

RELATED WORDS:
- {肯定形|こうていけい}: affirmative form
- {否定形|ひていけい}: negative form
- {活用形|かつようけい}: conjugated form — the general term for all verb forms
- {命令|めいれい}: command, order — the base noun
